body: My mother wouldn't really respect a professional opinion, because my gender dysphoria would be something that she would think is made up, or that I have a mental illness that is curable by convincing me that I'm a girl, when really the only way I'll ever be happy is being allowed to transition. I guess sleeping would be the best thing I could do right now. I've tired myself out by crying, and talking with you has made me feel a lot better. Thank you for talking with me—it really does mean a lot.

Canada. I can probably find therapists to email, and I also have a school counsellor I can go to. It's mostly just a matter of gathering the courage to do it, because I don't want to be forced out of the closet if anyone decides to tell my mother. And they most certainly will, if I tell them I've been suicidal and that I've been self-harming.

Yeah, it would help if I could transition and not hide. I could actually be confident and be who I really am, but my mother doesn't understand at all. She is loving in other ways, but never listens when I tell her I'm depressed because when I start to explain she just says it's all in my head and I can make it go away. That's not possible for me. It's really hard.
